column1: # The SELF container, as three independent open-source projects read or write it.
# Columns: struct, field, offset, size, type, value, note
# The fourth source, a reader, confirms the writer independently, including the two fields a
# loader rejects a container without: `if not (flags & 0x800): continue` and
# `idx = (flags >> 20) & 0xFFF`. It also pins that the ELF begins at
# `0x20 + segment_count * 0x20`, immediately after the entry table with no padding.
# No vendor binary was read to produce this table, and none may be read to extend it. `titles/`
# holds packages to check output against, never to derive from.
# The sources describe the Orbis-generation container: OpenOrbis is an Orbis-generation
# toolchain and the readers are Orbis-generation loaders. Rows are IMPLEMENTATIONS-level except
# where a measurement below settles them, and a file built from this table is a hypothesis
# until the hardware accepts or rejects it.
# The fixed header rows against 32 containers installed on Prospero-generation hardware:
#   ptype 0x1 (PTYPE_FAKE)  9 containers   all nine fixed rows match this table
#   ptype 0x0              23 containers   the same five rows differ, identically, on every one
# The other four (`mode` 0x1, `endian` 0x1, `category` 0x1, `padding3` 0x0) hold on all 32 and
# each row says so in place. The table derives from OpenOrbis, a fake-SELF writer, so it
# In this sample authenticity and container kind coincide: every ptype 0x1 container is a
# `PPSA` game and every ptype 0x0 container an `NPXS` system application. The five rows may
# track fake-versus-genuine or application-versus-system. The fake reading is better supported
# (it is what the source wrote, and `ptype` is the field for it) but not established; a genuine
# application container or a fake system one would separate them. `mkself` emits the same five
# values at every privilege tier, since `Privilege` reaches only `paid` in `self_ex_info`.
#   settles: no non-fake container on the measured hardware matches these five rows, and all
#            nine fixed rows hold for fake ones. Does not settle whether the five track
#                     Prospero magic (54 14 F5 EE)   Orbis magic (4F 15 3D 1D)
# Every genuine container carries the Prospero-generation magic. The fakes span both values,
# so the hardware does not impose it; the correlation has the control group the five header
# rows lack. A title's eboot does not carry the Orbis-generation magic; the two that do are
# Both magics are accepted, each on its own delivery route:
#   Orbis magic     a package built with it installs, mounts, loads and executes
#   Prospero magic  a native title directory whose eboot carries it installs, launches and runs
#                   to completion; the eboot was built by `mkself --generation 5` and read back
#                   by the census probe as one of the seven fake/Prospero entries above
# Because acceptance differs by route, there is no default magic: the pipeline requires
# `--target`, so every container built here names its magic by naming its machine (D100).
#   measured-by: obscene 048-selfaudit, payload and eboot legs
#   settles: genuine Prospero-generation containers carry the Prospero magic, 23 of 23, with
#            fakes on both sides as a control; a container built here with that magic is
#            accepted on the native-title route. Does not settle either magic on the other route.
# The tail layout `[... ex_info 64][npdrm 48]` ending at `header_size` comes from OpenOrbis, a
# writer; no reader supplies it. Seven containers not written from this table (six system apps
# Files of different sizes agreeing on three of four fields is not what a misaligned read
# gives, and the full census finds `ptype 0x0` and `npdrm.type 0x0` on all 23 genuine
# containers, so the offset is consistent with the measurement. `paid` varying per application
# fits a program authority id. `ptype 0x0` is not among the `ptype` values listed below, and
# `npdrm.type 0x0` (the table pins 0x3) reads as no npdrm control block; neither gets a row,
# since an unexplained value is not named.
#   settles: nothing about what the values mean; the tail is where this table says for seven
#            containers not written here, and they carry `ptype` 0x0 and no npdrm block.
# Two readers give the shape and one constant; the writer gives the blocks a loader skips
# (everything from `ex_info` down) and settles two things the readers leave open:
#   * bytes 4..7 - shadPS4 names four fields without values, fpPS4 gives `00 01 01 12` as one
#     word, OpenOrbis names them and gives the values. All three agree.
# Bytes 8..11: shadPS4 reads `category:u8, program_type:u8, padding1:u16`; OpenOrbis writes one
# `key_type:u32 = 0x101`. Little-endian those are the same bytes, `01 01 00 00`, so both
#   [self_header 32][entry 32 x N][ELF ehdr + phdrs][pad to 16][ex_info 64][npdrm 48]   <- header_size
#   [segment payloads, each aligned to 16]                                              <- from header_size + meta_size
# Two entries per segment: a digest entry carrying one 32-byte digest per BLOCK_SIZE block of
# the segment, then a data entry carrying the segment itself. `segment_count` is twice the
# number of qualifying program headers; the readers do not say so.
# Qualifying program header types: PT_LOAD, PT_SCE_RELRO, PT_SCE_DYNLIBDATA, PT_SCE_COMMENT.
# PT_SCE_VERSION is kept aside as version_data rather than becoming an entry.
# For a fake SELF every digest and the whole signature are zero, which is the same statement
# `meta_block` makes by being 80 zero bytes: nothing here is claiming to be signed.
# The magic differs by generation and only the first four bytes change; header size, segment
# size and layout are identical. orbistoun (`crates/orbistoun-elf/src/wrapper.rs`) records
# both from real material, and that both appear in one title: bundled modules use the
# Prospero-generation format, substituted stub libraries the Orbis-generation one.
#     Orbis generation     4F 15 3D 1D    <- what every source above describes
# `version_data` handling and the auth_info path `make_fself.py` takes are not described.
